inr.f: (hematology) Initialism of international normalized ratio (“indicator of the clotting tendency of blood”).

s.g: A small decorative box, hung from the sash of a kimono, for holding small objects.
(military, also figuratively) An advance into enemy territory, an attempted invasion; an encroachment, an incursion.
(figuratively, usually in the plural) Often followed by in, into, or on: initial progress made toward accomplishing a goal or solving a problem.
s.x: Three weeks into it, I am finally beginning to make inroads on this project.

s.g: (intransitive, archaic) To make advances or incursions.
(transitive, obsolete) To make an inroad into (something).
The initial flow of electricity into a component when it is switched on.
